company_items.summary: AutoZone reported fiscal Q4 EPS of $56.05 versus the Street's $54.03, but the beat was low quality — driven by 145 basis points of tariff refund tailwind to gross margins and a 105 basis point non-cash LIFO benefit. Domestic comps came in at plus 1.6 percent versus the Street's plus 3.1 percent, though management noted positive comp linearity during the quarter. Operating expenses rose 100 basis points year over year to 33.4 percent of sales, raising quality concerns despite the headline beat.

MillerKnoll reported solid fiscal Q1 EPS of 53 cents versus the Street's 36 cents, and critically the beat holds up even excluding tariff refunds — stripping out the 11-cent tailwind still leaves EPS of 42 cents versus the 36-cent consensus. Guidance is mixed with fiscal 2027 sales range trimmed but EPS outlook left unchanged.

THOR Industries missed fiscal Q4 EPS at 78 cents versus the Street's 87 cents as gross margin weakness — down 230 basis points year over year to 12.4 percent versus the 13.85 percent estimate — more than offset slightly better-than-expected revenue of $2.311 billion versus the $2.17 billion estimate. Management cited the difficult macro landscape. This is a negative read on the RV consumer and discretionary spending broadly.

Meta's Muse personal AI agent is seeing surging downloads ahead of Zuckerberg's keynote at the Meta Connect conference Wednesday night at 7pm ET, with investor expectations growing increasingly bullish. Shopify announced it will allow Muse to complete purchases on its e-commerce platform, a significant commerce integration that stands in contrast to Amazon's decision to block Muse from its storefront.

Shopify will allow Meta's Muse personal AI agent to complete purchases on its e-commerce platform, positioning Shopify as the preferred agentic commerce destination over Amazon. This is a meaningful partnership that could drive incremental transaction volume through Shopify's merchant base.

Quest Diagnostics shares were hit Tuesday following new Medicare payment rates from CMS for lab services that represented a larger reduction than the market had anticipated. The rate cuts are a direct headwind to revenue and margins for the lab testing business.

LabCorp shares fell alongside Quest Diagnostics after CMS released new Medicare lab service payment rates that came in worse than expected. Both companies face a direct earnings headwind from the larger-than-anticipated reimbursement cuts.

Cognex announced it will acquire RealSense, described as the market leader in depth-sensing cameras and vision technology for robotic perception and Physical AI, for approximately $500 million upfront plus an additional $106.5 million. The deal expands Cognex's capabilities into Physical AI and robotics perception at a time when demand for automation vision systems is accelerating.

Alibaba unveiled what it called China's most powerful AI chip and hinted at plans to train a model with up to 10 trillion parameters. Management also outlined plans to operate more than 20 gigawatts of data center capacity by 2032, signaling an aggressive infrastructure buildout in the AI race.

Viking Therapeutics reported positive trial results for its GLP-1 drug VK2735, showing 22 percent weight loss in trial participants. This is a meaningful clinical readout that reinforces Viking as a credible competitor in the high-stakes obesity drug market.

tts_summary:
Here's your midday read for Tuesday September 22nd.

The broad market is going nowhere fast. S&P 500 is flat, Nasdaq is up about 38 basis points, the Russell 2000 is up 30 basis points, and the Dow is lagging, down 43 basis points. Treasuries are flat across the curve. Brent is off modestly around a hundred dollars a barrel as investors hold out hope for a diplomatic resolution at the United Nations — Iran has reportedly signaled it could reopen the Strait of Hormuz within seven days if the US takes initial steps to ease military pressure, and Saudi Arabia's East-West Pipeline appears to be coming back online at least partially. So energy risk is fading at the margin, which is a modest positive for the macro backdrop.

On the company side, the big story is the AI setup going into the next week and a half. Meta's Muse personal AI agent is seeing surging downloads heading into Zuckerberg's keynote Wednesday night at seven pm Eastern. And Shopify announced it will allow Muse to complete purchases on its platform — a significant commerce integration that Amazon specifically blocked. That Shopify-Meta angle is worth watching closely. Alibaba also dropped news overnight, unveiling what it's calling China's most powerful AI chip and teasing a model with up to ten trillion parameters along with a plan to run more than twenty gigawatts of data center capacity by 2032. That's a massive infrastructure commitment. OpenAI DevDay hits on the 29th and Micron reports on the 30th — so the AI catalyst calendar is stacked.

On earnings, AutoZone beat on fiscal Q4 EPS but the quality was poor — most of the upside came from tariff refunds and a LIFO accounting benefit while domestic comps missed at plus one point six percent versus the Street's plus three point one percent. MillerKnoll was the cleaner beat — fifty-three cents versus thirty-six expected, and the beat holds up even stripping out tariff refund help. Thor Industries missed and management called the macro landscape difficult, which is a cautionary note on the RV consumer. Viking Therapeutics reported positive GLP-1 trial data showing twenty-two percent weight loss, keeping them in the obesity drug conversation.

On the negative side, Quest Diagnostics and LabCorp are both getting hit on CMS Medicare lab rate cuts that came in worse than expected. Financials are broadly underperforming — banks, brokers, insurers, asset managers all in the red — which is a notable risk-off signal underneath an otherwise mixed surface. And data center sentiment is taking a hit as the Texas governor halted new data center permitting, and a clean energy company delayed its IPO citing cooling enthusiasm for the space.

Tonight after the close watch KBH and WOR earnings. The bigger setup is Wednesday night with the Meta keynote. The market is in a holding pattern but the AI catalyst runway ahead is real — stay focused on that thread.
